Note on the text. Translated from the Italian original. The signs [?] mark passages that are uncertain or damaged in the original.

“Holiness, I want to do the will of God.”

On 30 August, her name day, while her soul was so deeply pierced…, her Sisters and the Novices of Piacenza wished to give her a little celebration. That was the occasion on which she poured into the souls of her Daughters the fullness of her mother’s heart, as though making her spiritual testament:

“Truly,” she said, “your expressions of affection have moved me. First of all I thank the Superior, who, heedless of the effort, with all her affection took pains to celebrate this day. And I thank you too, my beloved daughters; I have always believed in your affection, but today more than ever, gathered here together, you show me how much you love me. Yes, love the Mother; love her in Holy Church; love her in Mother Saint Anne. I am ashamed that the Holy Mother still upholds me, that she still, in her kindness, keeps turning her motherly eyes upon me. For in the breadth of this Institute the mission is great, and many are the circumstances that continually wear down these poor limbs. Physical pains, contradictions, anxieties and anguish would long ago have made me give way […] truly, my daughters, whatever you see that is great in the Institute, do not think that it is I; no, you owe it to the Holy Mother. I am nothing but a most unworthy creature […]. Another creature far more worthy, one who would have done more good than I, ought to have been chosen to spread this Institute and to guide you, who are all angels, all beautiful souls. I am the vilest creature, the most wretched, but the good God and the Holy Mother turned their compassionate gaze upon me and did great things in me. I work, I toil, but it is wholly the divine power that dwells in me; unworthy as I am, drained of strength, I spend myself entirely for you, and I will never fail my vocation. Daughters, I want one promise from you on this day: that you be faithful to the Institute and to Holy Mother Church. No, my daughters, let neither slander, nor anxieties, nor anguish make you fail in your holy vocation, in the sublime grace you have received from God.

I too was slandered, despised, ill-treated, and yet not the slightest thought against my holy vocation ever came to me. Be strong against every assault, fight valiantly and you will come out victorious. Keep always in mind the words I speak to you at this moment; put them into practice and you will find contentment. Daughters, when obedience seems too hard to you, when it wants you in America, in distant lands, obey willingly; better a thousand deaths than to fail in holy obedience […]. Look to the Crucified when tribulations assail you: and who suffered more than He? […]. He will be our strength, our guide. He will fight with us and be our courage […]. I love you all in God, I hold you close to my heart, and I spend myself in everything at your service. I cannot say more; my one thought is God alone, my only support, and no one will be able to draw me away from Him. I love you, my daughters, but in God, in that immense love that abides in every heart: be grateful, dear daughters. Pray for me, and I will keep you engraved upon my heart. God bless you!”
